sweep.heading: What sweep 9 found, in one paragraph
sweep.text: Alabama regulates less than the compilations implied and the Code says so plainly. The salary-history provision in § 25-1-30 bars only retaliation for declining to give wage history; there is no inquiry ban, and the 2023 bill that would have added one died in committee. The 2016 restrictive-covenant act presumes two years reasonable for an employee noncompete and eighteen months for a customer non-solicit, puts the burden on the enforcing party and leaves job skills alone unprotectable. No posting law, mini-WARN, private-employer fair-chance statute, credit-check limit, AI-hiring statute or stay-or-pay restriction exists, and the medical-cannabis act disclaims any employer duty. What the state does require is E-Verify of every employer since April 2012 under the Beason-Hammon Act, new-hire reporting within seven days, child-labor certificates, and a voluntary drug-free workplace program that buys a five percent workers' compensation discount. The programs are real and mostly free: AIDT recruits, screens and trains at no cost to the employer under its own statute, the Jobs Act pays a cash rebate of up to three percent of payroll for ten years with new project agreements open until mid-2028, Innovate Alabama matches SBIR and STTR awards, the Department of Workforce reimburses up to three quarters of on-the-job training wages, and the apprenticeship credit expired at the end of 2024. The numbers now sit beside their national twins: Alabama unemployment at 3.5 percent and Huntsville's at 3.0 against the nation's 4.2 in the latest months, Huntsville's professional and business services employment up 5 percent in a year, Madison County's average weekly wage of $1,596 against Alabama's $1,292, and aerospace engineers in Huntsville at forty-two times the national concentration. On the defense side the Trusted Workforce quarterly puts continuous-vetting enrollment at 78 percent, GAO finds initial Top Secret investigations at 206 days against a 114-day goal and more than 12,500 cleared facilities overseen by 470 staff, CMMC became an award condition on November 10, 2025 with its second phase a year later, and the EO 11246 regulations leave the CFR on October 26, 2026 while the VEVRAA and Section 503 plans remain. The caveats: eight Alabama sections were read on a mirror of the Code because the official viewer is a script the fetch layer cannot run, no BLS series was proven through the API from this side of the proxy, and no government count of the cleared population newer than 2019 exists.
